title: Chilaquiles Verde Bake
subtitle: Tortilla chips baked in green salsa with eggs, crema, and cotija.
description: Adapted from classic Mexican chilaquiles verde tradition for a hotel-pan breakfast bake: sturdy tortilla chips tossed in simmered tomatillo salsa, baked until edges crisp, then topped with baked eggs and crema for ten portions.

ingredients.name: cotija cheese
ingredients.notes: crumbled, plus cilantro and radish slices

steps.title: Gather ingredients and equipment
steps.instruction: Line up every ingredient for Chilaquiles Verde Bake in the order you will cook — measure spices into ramekins, trim proteins on a dedicated board, and set tongs, thermometers, and hotel pans within arm's reach before any heat goes on.

steps.title: Preheat ovens and surfaces
steps.instruction: Preheat ovens, griddles, or grills to recipe temp before the crew arrives — cold equipment extends cook time and dries out batch Eggs. Confirm burners ignite evenly and sheet pans are greased or lined.

steps.title: Roast and blend salsa
steps.instruction: Roast tomatillos, onion, and jalapeños on a sheet pan at 425°F until charred in spots, about 12 minutes. Blend with broth until smooth, then simmer in a pot 10 minutes until slightly thickened. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Heat the oven
steps.instruction: Heat oven to 375°F. Grease a deep hotel pan or two 9x13 dishes. Warm salsa off heat—you want it hot but not boiling when it hits the chips. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Toss chips with salsa
steps.instruction: Toss chips with just enough warm salsa to coat—about two-thirds of the batch. Reserve remaining salsa for serving. Chips should look sauced but not swimming or they will turn to mush. Plan about 5 minutes for this step at crew scale. Keep a backup tray at 200°F for firefighters returning from a call — never serve picked-over pans to late crew.

steps.title: Bake and add eggs
steps.instruction: Spread chips in the pan and bake 8 minutes. Make ten wells, crack an egg into each, and bake 10–12 more minutes until whites are set (165°F) and yolks are jammy. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Verify safe internal temps
steps.instruction: Spot-check the thickest pieces with an instant-read thermometer — target 165°F. If any piece reads low, return it to heat immediately rather than holding under temp on the line.

steps.title: Hold for call interruptions
steps.instruction: If tones drop mid-service, cover finished food and hold at 140°F in a warm cabinet or 200°F oven — never leave proteins below 140°F for more than 30 minutes cumulative. Note the hold time on the pan with a grease pencil.

steps.title: Finish and portion
steps.instruction: Drizzle crema in zigzags, scatter cotija and cilantro, and serve with reserved warm salsa and lime wedges. Portion with a wide spatula to keep layers intact. Plan about 5 minutes for this step at crew scale. Keep a backup tray at 200°F for firefighters returning from a call — never serve picked-over pans to late crew.

stationWorkflow: Use thick chips only—thin restaurant chips dissolve before eggs finish baking.
Hold extra salsa warm for crew members who want a saucier plate at the line.
Cut radishes and cilantro while the first bake runs so garnish is ready at the oven door.
cleanupNotes: Soak the hotel pan immediately with hot water—baked salsa and cheese glue sets fast.
Rinse the blender with warm water before tomatillo skins dry inside the jar.
leftovers: Chilaquiles soften overnight; re-crisp on a sheet pan at 375°F for 8 minutes before reheating.
Fold leftovers into breakfast burritos with scrambled eggs and extra hot salsa.
